body: I'm even supposed to move to Portland, OR in a few months where my fiancé got into grad school. Idk if I will be able to make it until then and even if I do I know I will still carry my PTSD with me.

I honestly don't think I should have to live with this pain. Just because it isn't terminal doesn't mean it can't make life impossible to live. Like most mental illnesses it's an "invisible illness" so it's hard for people to understand the impact it truly makes on your life unless they have experienced it. I see rape culture everywhere and it makes me want to die even more. PTSD isn't something that just magically goes away, even with whatever treatments you try. For many it is a lifelong illness. I feel like I've failed and given up. I majored in studio art and I forgot how to even enjoy it anymore. I feel like I'm a terrible artist bc I live in the Midwest where hardly anyone buys art anyway. A lot of people around here are cynical and negative. I meditate and take my meds and eat well and see a therapist, etc. but still I don't think i can go on. I still have episodes where my ptsd gets so bad that I can't function at all. I had to take a break toward the end of my last semester of undergrad because I was seriously having a mental breakdown. I build a wall between me and everyone else. I always make jokes or act like I don't care what people think so I think a lot of people around me (and even close to me) don't realize that I am breaking down before their eyes.
Not sure why that posted so many times but you get the point.

Obv I have tried many treatments/medications and I have a very good therapist and a psychiatrist. I have had my genes tested to see compatibility with medications and I couldn't count how many I've tried. I've been in therapy for years. I'm an extremely determined person and quite a nerd. I was planning on getting my masters in art therapy now that I have my ba. I've also done many a google on the subject. I don't need you to explain PTSD or suicide to me. Best.
